featured_videos.title: This Is The New Butter (And You’ll Be FORCED To Eat It!)
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Is The New Butter (And You’ll Be FORCED To Eat It!)
featured_videos.commentary: Okay, so the community is basically saying "local farms or bust," and honestly, they're onto something. The butter conversation is hitting different on carnivore. we're already watching ingredient lists like hawks, and this just confirms why. The frustration in these comments isn't conspiracy brain, it's people who've literally felt the difference between real butter and what's on most grocery shelves. If you're not already sourcing from local farms or reading every label, this is your sign. The system's broken, but your kitchen doesn't have to be.

featured_videos.title: This Carnivore Recipe Destroyed My Carb Cravings
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: This Carnivore Recipe Destroyed My Carb Cravings
featured_videos.commentary: Most people don't realize cravings aren't really about the food, they're about the texture and satisfaction your brain is craving. When you find a carnivore recipe that actually *delivers* on that level, it changes everything, and honestly it's one of the biggest reasons people stick with this way of eating long-term. The fact that it's cheap to make and doesn't require some complicated skill set? That's the real win here. Budget-friendly meals that actually work are what keep people from falling back into old patterns when life gets busy.

featured_videos.title: 93% Buy Meat At Costco Wrong (Buy This Instead!)
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: 93% Buy Meat At Costco Wrong (Buy This Instead!)
featured_videos.commentary: The marbling conversation in the comments is real. People aren't just looking for the cheapest cut anymore, they're learning to spot the difference between high Choice and low Prime, which honestly changes everything when you're buying in bulk. And yeah, the lamb comment caught me off guard too, but it tracks, people forget Costco's grass-fed lamb is legitimately one of the best protein-per-dollar plays they have. What's interesting here is that this isn't just about price anymore, it's about quality literacy. Three years ago carnivore meant "buy whatever meat is cheapest." Now the community's actually picking through cases, understanding fat content, and getting selective. That shift means people are staying on the diet longer because they're not getting bored with mediocre cuts.

featured_videos.title: Why Everyone’s Leaving Carnivore
featured_videos.creator: Shawn Baker MD
featured_videos.commentary: The people staying on carnivore aren't leaving because they're missing carbs or because they heard scary news. They're staying because they stopped hurting. That's the pattern you see in the comments, over and over. One person mentions arthritis flare-ups disappearing. Another talks about finally being pain-free after years of chronic disease. A third points out that any time they slip off, they feel terrible enough to come right back. That's not willpower or stubbornness, that's your body telling you the truth about what works for it. The noise around "why people quit" usually ignores the people who actually stayed, and what their experience shows.

featured_videos.title: I'm Eating This ENTIRE Pizza Everyday and Losing Weight
featured_videos.creator: Steak and Butter Gal
featured_videos.editorial_title: I'm Eating This ENTIRE Pizza Everyday and Losing Weight
featured_videos.commentary: This is exactly what people need to see. The comments are flooded with folks saying things like "pizza is my hardest food to give up" and "I've reversed heart disease and lost 60 pounds," which tells you something important: comfort food replacements aren't just nice to have, they're actually critical for staying on track long-term. What makes this different from the usual almond flour nonsense is that it's simple, it works, and it tastes legitimately good without requiring a pantry full of specialty ingredients. The cottage cheese base is clever because it's just food, not some processed substitute. If you've been thinking carnivore means never eating something satisfying again, this proves you wrong.

featured_videos.title: Carnivore/Lion Diet Update: Not Carnivore Anymore?
featured_videos.creator: Mikhaila Peterson
featured_videos.editorial_title: Carnivore/Lion Diet Update: Not Carnivore Anymore?
featured_videos.commentary: This is the conversation we need to be having more often. Mikhaila's been the face of "never eating plants again," so watching her expand her diet after eight years takes guts. and it's honest. The lion diet got her to remission, which is incredible, but she's showing us that strict elimination isn't always the final destination. It's a tool. For a lot of people reading this, that's permission they didn't know they needed. You can use carnivore to heal, hit reset, figure out what your body actually tolerates. Then you get to make choices instead of being trapped by fear. That's the real win.
